title: Consolidate System lowering into a single pass with a core Lifetime value type
description:
## Problem Statement

Lowering an authored **System** from its Protocol Buffer representation into an executable `CameraSystem` (AST structure plus externalized `TransformParams` keyed by `TransformIndex`) currently splits the **Blend** layout rules across multiple independent traversals:

1. One traversal builds the `ast::Transform` tree (`pre` **Affine Transform**, `WeightedSumTransform` of **Formulas**, `post` **Affine Transform**, and **Coloring Method** expression, plus enabled-**Blend** filtering and **Isolated Blend** selection).
2. A second traversal re-derives the exact same conditional branches to walk `TransformIndex` (`firstChild`, `nextSibling`, `parent`) and populate `TransformParams`.
3. The **Formula** preview generator constructs a third, hand-indexed `MultiStepTransform` with literal `TransformIndex{0}` and `TransformIndex{1}` paths.
4. **Particle** **Lifetime** rules (`[Min, Max]` or `Infinite`) are split across the QML editor, `SystemModel`, `SystemView`, and `SystemProcessor`, and **Lifetime** is passed to the generator over a separate side channel (`setLifetimeRange`) after `setSystem`. Because `SystemModel::setMinLifetime` compares `min > max_lifetime` directly, editing `minLifetime` while `isInfiniteLifetime` is active (`max_lifetime == -1`) is broken and rejects every non-negative value.
5. Unchecked inputs in loaded or hand-edited **Project** files—such as an unrecognized **Formula** type string or an out-of-range **Isolated Blend** index—throw or read out of bounds on the GUI thread during lowering, and invalid **Lifetime** values only log a console warning without normalizing the state or informing the user in the UI.

## Solution

Consolidate **System** and **Blend** lowering into a single-pass lowering module and introduce a dedicated `Lifetime` value type carried directly inside `CameraSystem`:

- A single-pass lowering builder walks each **Blend** and **System** once, emitting AST nodes and claiming their corresponding `TransformIndex` parameter slots simultaneously so structure and parameter indices cannot drift apart.
- Expose single-**Blend** lowering (`toTransformSystem`) alongside full **System** lowering (`toCameraSystem`) so the **Formula** preview provider reuses the same lowering module instead of hardcoding `TransformIndex` paths.
- Introduce a `Lifetime` value type in `core` that enforces the `[Min, Max]` / `Infinite` invariant, normalizes out-of-range values when needed, and encapsulates initial random **Lifetime** assignment vs. deterministic revived **Lifetime** assignment (per ADR-0003).
- Embed `Lifetime` inside `CameraSystem` so `CameraSystemProcessor` applies it automatically and the separate `setLifetimeRange` channel across `Generator`, `HistogramGenerator`, and `BlenderTask` is removed.
- Make lowering resilient: sanitize invalid `Lifetime` bounds, skip unrecognized **Formula** types (omitting `WeightedSumTransform` if no valid **Formulas** remain), and fall back to enabled **Blends** when an **Isolated Blend** index is out of range, while recording human-readable warning messages that are logged and surfaced to the user via the main window's `Snackbar`.
- Update `SystemModel` to enforce the same `Lifetime` rules in the UI, fixing the bug where `minLifetime` cannot be edited when **Lifetime** is `Infinite`.

## User Stories

1. As a fractal author, I want to edit the minimum **Particle** **Lifetime** while **Lifetime** is set to `Infinite`, so that I can control the number of unplotted warm-up iterations even when **Particles** never expire.
2. As a fractal author, I want the UI to reject negative `minLifetime` values and `maxLifetime` values below `1` (unless `Infinite`), so that I cannot accidentally configure an invalid **Lifetime** range from the editor.
3. As a fractal author, I want `minLifetime` to automatically clamp down to `maxLifetime` when I switch from `Infinite` (or a larger maximum) to a finite `maxLifetime` smaller than the current `minLifetime`, so that the `[Min, Max]` invariant is always preserved.
4. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file that contains an unrecognized **Formula** type, I want ChaosKit to skip that **Formula**, continue rendering the rest of the **Blend**, and show a warning in the `Snackbar`, so that the application does not crash on the GUI thread.
5. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file where every **Formula** in a **Blend** has an unrecognized type, I want the **Blend** to lower cleanly with only its `pre` and `post` **Affine Transforms** and **Coloring Method** intact, so that the remaining steps still receive their expected parameter slots.
6. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file with an out-of-range **Isolated Blend** index, I want ChaosKit to fall back to rendering all enabled **Blends** and show a warning in the `Snackbar`, so that an invalid isolation index does not cause an out-of-bounds read.
7. As a fractal author opening a `.ck` **Project** file with invalid **Lifetime** numbers (such as negative `min_lifetime`, non-positive finite `max_lifetime`, or `min_lifetime > max_lifetime`), I want ChaosKit to clamp the **Lifetime** into a valid range and show a warning in the `Snackbar`, so that the **System** still renders safely.
8. As a fractal author viewing **Formula** previews in the picker, I want the preview renderer to lower its example `pre` **Affine Transform** and **Formula** through the standard **Blend** lowering module, so that previews always match the parameter-slot layout used by the main renderer.
9. As a fractal author adjusting **Lifetime** settings, I want newly created **Particles** to receive a randomized initial **Lifetime** while revived **Particles** receive the full `maxLifetime` (per ADR-0003), so that startup transients are smoothed while **Lifetime** adjustments remain visually predictable.
10. As a developer maintaining ChaosKit, I want AST structure construction and `TransformIndex` parameter slot assignment for a **Blend** to happen in a single pass, so that changing how a **Blend** lowers only requires editing one traversal.
11. As a developer maintaining ChaosKit, I want `CameraSystem` to carry its `Lifetime` value directly, so that updating a **System** on a processor or generator updates its **Transform**, **Camera**, and **Lifetime** atomically through one interface.

## Implementation Decisions

- **`core::Lifetime` value type**:
  - Represents a **Particle** **Lifetime** range `[min, max]` where `max` is either a positive integer (`>= 1`) or `INFINITE_LIFETIME` (`-1`), and `min >= 0` with `min <= max` whenever `max` is finite.
  - Default value is `min = 0`, `max = INFINITE_LIFETIME`.
  - Provides a normalizing factory/constructor that clamps `min = std::max(0, min)`, treats `max == INFINITE_LIFETIME` as infinite while clamping any other `max < 1` to `1`, and clamps `min = std::min(min, max)` when finite, reporting whether normalization occurred so callers can emit a warning.
  - Provides helper methods for **Particle** lifecycle management following ADR-0003:
    - Initial **Particle** **Lifetime** draw: returns `INFINITE_LIFETIME` when infinite, otherwise `rng.randomInt(std::min(min + 1, max), max)`.
    - Revived **Particle** **Lifetime**: returns `max` (which is `INFINITE_LIFETIME` when infinite).
    - Warm-up count: returns `min`.
  - Supports equality comparison (`==`, `!=`) and debug stream output (`operator<<`).
- **Embedding `Lifetime` in `core::CameraSystem`**:
  - Add `Lifetime lifetime` as a field on `core::CameraSystem` (included in `operator==` / `operator!=` and debug printing).
  - `CameraSystemProcessor` initializes its `SystemProcessor` `Lifetime` from `CameraSystem::lifetime` in its constructor and updates it inside `setCameraSystem(const CameraSystem&)`.
  - `SystemProcessor` stores a `Lifetime` member instead of separate raw `min_lifetime_` / `max_lifetime_` integers (retaining convenience setters/getters on `SystemProcessor` where useful for direct unit tests).
  - Remove `setLifetimeRange(int32_t, int32_t)` from `core::Generator`, `ui::HistogramGenerator`, and `ui::BlenderTask`, and remove the separate `generator_->setLifetimeRange(...)` call from `SystemView::updateSystem()`.
- **Single-pass lowering in `ui/storage/conversions`**:
  - Replace the separate `toTransform` and `populateParams` / `toParams` traversals with a single-pass builder that tracks the current `core::TransformIndex` while constructing `ast::Transform` nodes and writing parameter vectors into `core::TransformParams` at the same time.
  - Expose two functions in `ui/storage/conversions`:
    - `core::TransformSystem toTransformSystem(const Blend& blendProto, std::vector<std::string>* warnings = nullptr)`
    - `core::CameraSystem toCameraSystem(const System& systemProto, std::vector<std::string>* warnings = nullptr)`
  - When lowering a **Blend**:
    - If `has_pre()`, emit `ast::AffineTransform` and claim the current child `TransformIndex` for its 6 matrix parameters.
    - For `formulas()`, resolve each `Formula::type()` via `magic_enum::enum_cast<library::FormulaType>`. If a type is unrecognized (or `FormulaType::Invalid`), append a warning message (if `warnings != nullptr`) and skip it. Only if at least one valid **Formula** remains, emit `ast::WeightedSumTransform` at the next step `TransformIndex` and assign each valid **Formula**'s parameters to its corresponding child `TransformIndex`.
    - If `has_post()`, emit `ast::AffineTransform` and claim the next sibling `TransformIndex` for its 6 matrix parameters.
    - If `has_coloring_method()`, attach the corresponding coloring expression to the `MultiStepTransform` and store its scalar parameter at the **Blend**'s parent `TransformIndex`.
  - When lowering a **System**:
    - Normalize `(min_lifetime, max_lifetime)` into `core::Lifetime`; if normalization adjusted either bound, record a warning message.
    - If `has_isolated_blend()`, check whether `isolated_blend().index()` is within `[0, blends_size())`. If valid, lower only that **Blend** at the root `TransformIndex`. If out of bounds, record a warning message and fall back to lowering all enabled **Blends** inside a `RandomChoiceTransform`.
    - If `has_camera()` and `camera().enabled()`, lower `camera()` via `toTransformSystem(systemProto.camera(), warnings)`.
- **Reuse in `FormulaPreviewProvider`**:
  - In `FormulaPreviewProvider`, build a temporary `Blend` proto with the example `pre` **Affine Transform** and single **Formula** with weight `1.0` and example parameters, and lower it through `toTransformSystem` rather than manually constructing `TransformIndex{0}` and `TransformIndex{1}`.
- **`SystemModel` validation and UI warning surfacing**:
  - In `SystemModel::setMinLifetime(int min)`: reject `min < 0`; if `!isInfiniteLifetime()`, reject `min > maxLifetime()`; allow any `min >= 0` when `isInfiniteLifetime()` is true.
  - In `SystemModel::setMaxLifetime(int max)`: reject `max < 1` unless `max == core::SystemParticle::INFINITE_LIFETIME`; when `max` is finite and `minLifetime() > max`, clamp `min_lifetime` down to `max` and emit `minLifetimeChanged()`.
  - When `SystemView::updateSystem()` lowers the **System** proto via `toCameraSystem(systemProto, &warnings)`, log any warning messages with `qCWarning` and surface them to the user via a signal wired to `openSnackbar(...)` in `MainWindow.qml`.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test**:
  - Tests should exercise modules through their public interfaces (`toCameraSystem`, `toTransformSystem`, `SystemProcessor`, `CameraSystemProcessor`, and `SystemModel`) and assert observable outputs (`CameraSystem` values, `Particle` states after stepping with a deterministic `Rng`, emitted signals, and collected warning strings), not internal helper functions.
- **Modules to be tested**:
  - `ui/storage/conversions`:
    - Existing tests in `conversions_test` updated to verify that `CameraSystem` includes the expected `Lifetime`.
    - New tests in `conversions_test` for `toTransformSystem(const Blend&)`.
    - New tests for fallback and warning collection: unknown **Formula** type alongside a valid **Formula**, a **Blend** where all **Formulas** are unknown (verifying `post` still lands at the right `TransformIndex`), out-of-range `isolated_blend` index falling back to enabled **Blends**, and invalid `min_lifetime` / `max_lifetime` clamping with warnings.
    - Behavioral round-trip test: lower a `System` with `pre`, **Formula**, `post`, **Coloring Method**, and **Camera**, run a **Particle** through `CameraSystemProcessor`, and assert the resulting **Particle** coordinates and **Color Coordinate** (verifying that lowered `TransformIndex` slots match `TransformInterpreter`).
  - `core::Lifetime`, `core::SystemProcessor`, and `core::CameraSystemProcessor`:
    - Unit tests for `Lifetime` normalization and invariants.
    - Existing `SystemProcessorTest` suite (preserving `CreatesParticleWithRandomLifetime*` and `RevivesDeadParticle*` per ADR-0003).
    - Test in `CameraSystemProcessorTest` verifying that `CameraSystem::lifetime` is applied when constructing or updating `CameraSystemProcessor`.
  - `ui::SystemModel`:
    - Unit test verifying `setMinLifetime` succeeds when `isInfiniteLifetime` is true, rejects negative values, rejects `min > max` when finite, and clamps `minLifetime` when `setMaxLifetime` lowers a finite `max` below `min`.
- **Prior art**:
  - `ui/storage/conversions_test.cpp`, `core/SystemProcessorTest.cpp`, and `core/CameraSystemProcessorTest.cpp` (GoogleTest / GoogleMock).

## Out of Scope

- Refactoring `HistogramGenerator`, `BlenderTask`, `GathererTask`, and `SimpleHistogramGenerator` into a Qt-free render session (tracked in `chaoskit-9gb`).
- Automatic child registration and change-kind propagation in `BaseModel` (tracked in `chaoskit-fth`).
- Managing `isolated_blend` index updates on **Blend** deletion in `SystemModel` and centralizing authoring defaults (tracked in `chaoskit-fu9`).
- Changing the initial random **Lifetime** vs. deterministic revived **Lifetime** behavior (recorded in ADR-0003).
close_reason: Consolidated System lowering into a single pass and introduced core Lifetime value type

title: Core Lifetime value type and CameraSystem integration
description:
## Parent

chaoskit-94f

## What to build

Introduce a dedicated `core::Lifetime` value type in `core/Lifetime.h` (and `core/Lifetime.cpp` if needed) enforcing the `[Min, Max]` / `Infinite` invariant, input normalization, initial random lifetime assignment, and deterministic revived lifetime assignment per ADR-0003. Embed `Lifetime` directly in `CameraSystem`, and update `SystemProcessor` and `CameraSystemProcessor` to accept and apply `Lifetime` directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `core::Lifetime` struct/class encapsulates `min_lifetime` and `max_lifetime` with methods `min()`, `max()`, and `isInfinite()`
- [ ] `Lifetime` constructor or factory validates/normalizes: clamp negative `min` to 0; if not infinite, ensure `max >= 1`; if finite and `min > max`, clamp `min` to `max`
- [ ] `Lifetime::normalize(int32_t min, int32_t max, bool* adjusted = nullptr)` provides explicit normalization logic returning normalized `Lifetime` and indicating if adjustments were made
- [ ] `Lifetime` encapsulates `createParticleLifetime(Rng&)` drawing from `[min(min + 1, max), max]` (or infinite) and `revivedLifetime()` returning `max` (or infinite) and `warmup = min` per ADR-0003
- [ ] `CameraSystem` contains `Lifetime lifetime` field and equality operators account for it
- [ ] `CameraSystemProcessor` applies `cameraSystem.lifetime` on construction and `setCameraSystem`
- [ ] Unit tests in `LifetimeTest` verify invariant enforcement, normalization, and ADR-0003 lifetime generation
- [ ] Existing `SystemProcessorTest` suite continues to pass
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass
close_reason: Implemented core::Lifetime value type and integrated with CameraSystem

title: SystemModel lifetime validation and infinite lifetime editing fix
description:
## Parent

chaoskit-94f

## What to build

Update `SystemModel::setMinLifetime` and `SystemModel::setMaxLifetime` to fix the bug where `minLifetime` cannot be edited while `isInfiniteLifetime` is true, enforce valid lifetime bounds in the UI model, and automatically maintain the `[Min, Max]` invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SystemModel::setMinLifetime(int min)` allows editing any `min >= 0` when `isInfiniteLifetime()` is true
- [ ] `SystemModel::setMinLifetime(int min)` rejects `min < 0` and rejects `min > maxLifetime()` when finite
- [ ] `SystemModel::setMaxLifetime(int max)` rejects `max < 1` unless `max == core::SystemParticle::INFINITE_LIFETIME`
- [ ] When `max` is finite and `minLifetime() > max`, `SystemModel::setMaxLifetime` clamps `min_lifetime` down to `max` and emits `minLifetimeChanged()`
- [ ] Unit tests in `SystemModelTest` verify `setMinLifetime` with infinite lifetime, invalid inputs, and clamping behavior
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass
close_reason: Fixed infinite lifetime editing in SystemModel and added lifetime validation

title: Single-pass System and Blend lowering with resilience and warnings
description:
## Parent

chaoskit-94f

## What to build

Consolidate System and Blend lowering in `ui/storage/conversions` into a single-pass lowerer that walks the Protocol Buffer representation once, emitting AST nodes and claiming corresponding `TransformIndex` parameter slots simultaneously. Expose `toTransformSystem` (for single Blend) and `toCameraSystem` (for full System), accept a warnings collection, normalize `Lifetime` via `core::Lifetime`, skip unrecognized Formula types gracefully, and fall back on out-of-range isolated blend indices.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Lowering walks each `Blend` once, creating AST steps and claiming `TransformIndex` parameter slots in lockstep
- [ ] Expose `toTransformSystem(const Blend& blendProto, std::vector<QString>& warnings)` returning `core::TransformSystem`
- [ ] Update `toCameraSystem(const System& systemProto, std::vector<QString>& warnings)` to populate AST, parameters, and `Lifetime`
- [ ] Overload `toCameraSystem(const System& systemProto)` for backwards compatibility
- [ ] Normalize `(min_lifetime, max_lifetime)` into `core::Lifetime` inside `toCameraSystem`, recording a warning if normalization adjusted either bound
- [ ] If a `Formula` has an unrecognized type, skip it, record a warning, and if no valid formulas remain in the Blend, omit `ast::WeightedSumTransform` while preserving `pre`, `post`, and coloring method at correct `TransformIndex` slots
- [ ] If `isolated_blend` index is out of `[0, blends_size())`, record a warning and fall back to lowering all enabled blends in `RandomChoiceTransform`
- [ ] Existing `conversions_test` test cases pass with `CameraSystem::lifetime` verified
- [ ] New unit tests in `conversions_test` verify: `toTransformSystem(Blend)`, unknown formula skipping, all-unknown formulas blend, out-of-range isolated blend fallback, lifetime normalization warning, and behavioral round-trip through `CameraSystemProcessor`
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass
close_reason: Consolidated System lowering into single pass with resilience and warnings

title: Surface lowering warnings to Snackbar and remove setLifetimeRange channel
description:
## Parent

chaoskit-94f

## What to build

Capture warnings in `SystemView::updateSystem()` from `toCameraSystem`, log them via `qCWarning(systemViewLog)`, and emit a signal connected to `openSnackbar` in `MainWindow.qml`. Remove the obsolete `setLifetimeRange` channel across `Generator`, `HistogramGenerator`, `BlenderTask`, and `SimpleHistogramGenerator`, letting `CameraSystem::lifetime` carry lifetime configuration directly to the processor.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `SystemView` emits a signal (e.g. `warningEmitted(const QString& warning)`) when `toCameraSystem` produces warnings
- [ ] Warnings are logged via `qCWarning(systemViewLog)`
- [ ] `MainWindow.qml` connects `warningEmitted` to `openSnackbar(warning)`
- [ ] `generator_->setLifetimeRange(...)` is removed from `SystemView::updateSystem`
- [ ] `setLifetimeRange` is removed from `Generator`, `HistogramGenerator`, `BlenderTask`, and `SimpleHistogramGenerator`
- [ ] `BlenderTask` and `HistogramGenerator` rely entirely on `CameraSystem::lifetime`
- [ ] `make test` and `make lint` pass
close_reason: Surfaced lowering warnings to Snackbar and removed setLifetimeRange channel

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Rename Final Blend references to Camera across the protobuf schema, C++ models, conversions, and UI

**Current behavior:**
The codebase still uses legacy "Final Blend" terminology in multiple areas:
- `System` protobuf definition has `Blend final_blend = 2;`
- C++ classes (`SystemModel`, `ProjectModel`, `main.cpp`) access `final_blend()` and `mutable_final_blend()`
- Storage conversions and tests reference `has_final_blend()`, `final_blend()`, and test names like `ConvertsFinalBlendToCamera`
- `ui/resources.qrc` and `ui/forms` reference `FinalBlendIndicator.qml`

**Desired behavior:**
Align the codebase with the canonical domain terminology in `GLOSSARY.md` where Camera is the designated term:
- `final_blend` is renamed to `camera` in the `System` protobuf message (retaining field number 2)
- C++ model code, converters, and tests use `camera` / `mutable_camera()` / `has_camera()`
- Legacy references and filenames in `ui/forms` and `ui/resources.qrc` are renamed or retired
- Clean build and passing test suite

**Key interfaces:**
- `System` message in `chaoskit.proto`: `Blend camera = 2;`
- `SystemModel` & `ProjectModel`: bind `cameraBlend_` to `proto_->mutable_camera()`
- Storage converters (`conversions.cpp` / `conversions_test.cpp`): read from `systemProto.camera()` and verify transform/parameter mapping

- [ ] Protobuf message `System` has `Blend camera = 2;` and no `final_blend` field
- [ ] All usages of `mutable_final_blend()` and `final_blend()` in `ui/` are replaced with `camera()` and `mutable_camera()`
- [ ] Conversions and conversion unit tests use `camera` and all unit tests pass

title: Headless CLI renderer (chaoskit-render) and end-to-end golden image tests
description:
## Problem Statement

During development of ChaosKit, rendering a **Project** requires launching the interactive Qt Quick application, manually loading or configuring a **System**, waiting for **Particles** to accumulate into the **Histogram** over an unspecified wall-clock interval, and manually exporting the image. Because there is no headless command-line entry point that shares the Qt implementation's **Project** lowering, coordinate-to-pixel gathering, **Color Map** lookup, and OpenGL **Tone Mapping** pipeline, developers cannot quickly render **Projects** from the command line or write automated end-to-end tests that verify visual rendering output against known reference images (modulo stochastic simulation variance).

## Solution

Provide a standalone headless CLI executable (`chaoskit-render`) in a top-level CLI module that loads a serialized **Project** (in either binary Protobuf or human-readable Protobuf text format), optionally overrides **Project** rendering parameters via command-line flags, executes **Particle** simulation and **Histogram** accumulation using the shared Qt/core rendering components, runs the shared OpenGL **Tone Mapping** shader offscreen, and writes the resulting image to disk. By default, `chaoskit-render` runs multi-threaded across available hardware threads for fast image generation, and automatically switches to deterministic single-threaded execution when a random seed (`--seed`) is supplied. Accompanying end-to-end tests invoke `chaoskit-render` on checked-in **Project** fixtures and compare the rendered images against golden reference images using a perceptual/statistical error threshold (normalized RMSE).

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want to render a binary `.ck` **Project** saved from the Qt UI into an image file from the command line, so that I can inspect or batch-render authored **Projects** without opening the interactive UI.
2. As a developer, I want to render a human-readable Protobuf text-format **Project** from the command line, so that I can author, version-control, and review compact **Project** fixtures in Git.
3. As a developer, I want the CLI to reuse the Qt implementation's **Project**-to-execution lowering (`toCameraSystem`), aspect-ratio-preserving coordinate mapping and **Histogram** accumulation (`GathererTask`), **Color Map** registry, and OpenGL 3.2 Core **Tone Mapping** shader (`GLToneMapper`), so that CLI renders match the visual output of the interactive Qt UI.
4. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to run **Particle** stepping and **Histogram** gathering across all hardware threads by default without per-step lock contention, so that high-density renders complete as quickly as possible.
5. As a developer, I want to pass `--threads <N>` to explicitly control the number of worker threads during unseeded rendering, so that I can tune CPU utilization during local development or CI runs.
6. As a developer, I want passing `--seed <uint64>` to switch `chaoskit-render` into a single-threaded deterministic mode backed by a seeded PCG random number generator, so that repeated runs on the same platform produce identical **Histograms** and output images.
7. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to reject combining `--seed` with `--threads` greater than 1 with a clear error message and non-zero exit code, so that I am never misled into expecting deterministic output from a multi-threaded run.
8. As a developer, I want to control the simulation budget via `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>` (defaulting to a sensible density such as 100 plotted steps per pixel), so that rendering quality scales automatically with the **Project**'s image dimensions.
9. As a developer, I want to optionally specify an exact total count of plotted steps via `--iterations <N>` (mutually exclusive with `--ipp`), so that I can run fixed-workload renders regardless of resolution.
10. As a developer, I want each counted iteration in the CLI budget to represent one plotted **Particle** step (`process()` + `processCamera()`), so that configuring unplotted warm-up steps via minimum **Lifetime** does not starve the **Histogram** of plotted samples.
11. As a developer, I want to override the **Project**'s image `width` and `height` via `--width` and `--height` CLI flags, so that I can render thumbnails or high-resolution exports from the same **Project** file without modifying it.
12. As a developer, I want to override **Tone Mapping** parameters (`--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`) and the active **Color Map** (`--color-map`) via CLI flags, so that I can experiment with post-processing and color configurations from the command line.
13. As a developer, I want the CLI to apply the same fallback defaults as the Qt UI when `proto3` fields are unset/zero in a loaded **Project** (`width = 1024`, `height = 1024`, `gamma = 2.2`, and the registry's default **Color Map** when the **Color Map** name is empty), so that minimal text-format **Project** fixtures render identically to a default UI **Project**.
14. As a developer, I want all built-in **Color Maps** (`BlackWhite`, `Rainbow`, and `BGR`) to be registered in a single shared registry in the core module, so that any **Color Map** selectable in the Qt UI is also available in the CLI.
15. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to fail with a non-zero exit code and descriptive error message when a non-empty **Color Map** name is not found in the registry, when the input **Project** cannot be opened or parsed, or when the output image cannot be written, so that broken configurations fail fast in scripts and tests.
16. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to honor an **Isolated Blend** if present in the input **Project** (matching the Qt UI's lowering behavior) while emitting a warning to standard error, so that I can intentionally test blend isolation or immediately notice if a `.ck` file was accidentally saved with a soloed **Blend**.
17. As a developer, I want `chaoskit-render` to log any **System** lowering warnings (such as normalized **Lifetime** ranges or unrecognized **Formula** types) to standard error, so that authoring issues in **Project** fixtures are visible in CLI output.
18. As a developer, I want unhit background pixels (`point.w <= 0.0` in the **Histogram**) to evaluate to opaque black `vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` in the OpenGL **Tone Mapping** fragment shader instead of dividing `0.0 / 0.0` (`NaN`), so that background pixels render deterministically across GPU drivers and platforms.
19. As a developer, I want an automated CTest/GTest end-to-end test suite that runs `chaoskit-render` on checked-in **Project** fixtures and compares the output against golden PNG images using normalized RMSE, so that regressions in **Formula** evaluation, **Affine Transforms**, **Camera** projection, **Coloring Methods**, **Color Maps**, **Lifetime** handling, or **Tone Mapping** are caught by `make test`.
20. As a developer, I want failed end-to-end image comparisons to write `<test>_actual.png` and `<test>_diff.png` artifacts and support an environment variable (`CHAOSKIT_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1`) to regenerate golden images, so that I can easily inspect visual diffs and update reference images when intentional rendering changes are made.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Top-Level CLI Module & Executable Target**:
  - Introduce a new top-level `cli` module registered in the root CMake build, producing the `chaoskit-render` executable target and its end-to-end test target.
  - Link the CLI module against the existing `core`, `library`, `ui_core`, `ui_storage`, and `ui_colormapregistry` libraries without duplicating lowering, gathering, or shader code.
- **Shared Built-In Color Maps**:
  - Move registration of the `"BGR"` `PaletteColorMap` out of the UI application's `main()` into `core::ColorMapRegistry`'s constructor alongside `"BlackWhite"` and `"Rainbow"`, ensuring both the UI and CLI see the exact same built-in **Color Maps**.
  - Preserve `ColorMapRegistry::defaultName()`'s existing behavior (or guarantee `"BlackWhite"` is always present as fallback) when a **Project** has an empty **Color Map** name.
- **Project Loading & Normalization**:
  - Accept an input **Project** file in either binary Protobuf format or Protobuf `TextFormat` (attempting binary parse or text-format parse based on extension `.pbtxt`/`.cktxt` with fallback, rejecting files that fail both).
  - Normalize unset `proto3` zero values on the loaded `chaoskit::Project` before applying CLI overrides: if `width == 0`, set `1024`; if `height == 0`, set `1024`; if `gamma == 0.0f`, set `2.2f`. If `color_map.name` is empty, resolve to the registry's default **Color Map** name.
  - Apply any explicitly provided CLI override flags (`--width`, `--height`, `--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`, `--color-map`) on top of the normalized `chaoskit::Project`.
  - Lower `project.system()` via `ui::toCameraSystem()`, forwarding any emitted lowering warnings to `stderr`, and additionally emitting a warning to `stderr` if `system.has_isolated_blend()` is true.
- **CLI Argument Contract (`QCommandLineParser`)**:
  - Positional arguments: `<input-project>` and `<output-image>`.
  - Workload flags: `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>` (default `100`) and `--iterations <N>`. Passing both `--ipp` and `--iterations` is an error (non-zero exit). Total plotted steps is `ipp * width * height` when using `--ipp`, or `iterations` when using `--iterations`.
  - Concurrency & seeding flags: `--seed <uint64>` (optional, unset by default) and `--threads <N>` (optional, defaults to `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()` with a minimum of `1` when `--seed` is unset, and `1` when `--seed` is set). Passing both `--seed` and `--threads` with a value greater than `1` is rejected with a non-zero exit code.
  - Override flags: `--width <uint>`, `--height <uint>`, `--gamma <float>`, `--exposure <float>`, `--vibrancy <float>`, `--color-map <name>`.
- **Deterministic Seeded RNG & Multi-Threaded Histogram Gathering**:
  - Introduce a deterministic `core::Rng` implementation backed by `pcg32` initialized from a explicit `uint64_t` seed for `--seed` mode, while unseeded worker threads continue to use `core::ThreadLocalRng`.
  - Add a merge/accumulation operation on `core::HistogramBuffer` (and expose access to the underlying `core::HistogramBuffer` or merge method on `ui::GathererTask`) so each worker thread can own a thread-local `ui::GathererTask` and `core::CameraSystemProcessor`, step its assigned share of plotted steps in a tight loop without `QTimer` event-loop or mutex contention, and sum the per-thread `HistogramBuffer`s into a single combined `HistogramBuffer` on completion.
- **Headless OpenGL Tone Mapping & Image Export**:
  - Guard `point.w <= 0.0` in `ui::GLToneMapper`'s fragment shader to output `vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` early, preventing `0.0 / 0.0` (`NaN`) evaluation on unhit background pixels.
  - In `chaoskit-render`, initialize a `QGuiApplication`, create an OpenGL 3.2 Core `QSurfaceFormat`, `QOpenGLContext`, and `QOffscreenSurface`, bind a `QOpenGLFramebufferObject` of size `(width, height)`, run `ui::GLToneMapper` (`initializeGL()`, `setGamma()`, `setExposure()`, `setVibrancy()`, `syncBuffer()`, `map()`), read back the rendered `QImage` with vertical orientation matching `SystemView` in the Qt UI, and write it via `QImageWriter`.

## Testing Decisions

- **What Makes a Good Test**:
  - Tests must exercise only external behavior at the highest possible seam—never internal implementation details or private helper classes.
  - The entire feature is tested through a **single seam**: invoking the `chaoskit-render` CLI entry point (`(CLI args, input Project file) -> (exit code, stderr output, rendered output image file)`).
- **Modules Under Test**:
  - The `cli` module (`chaoskit-render`), along with its end-to-end integration across `ui_storage`, `ui_core`, `ui_colormapregistry`, `core`, and `library`.
  - Test cases at the CLI seam will cover:
    1. **End-to-end golden image verification**: Rendering representative `.pbtxt` / `.ck` **Project** fixtures (exercising multiple **Formulas**, **Affine Transforms**, **Blends**, **Camera**, **Coloring Methods**, **Color Maps**, **Lifetime** warm-up, and **Tone Mapping**) in both seeded single-threaded mode and unseeded multi-threaded mode, asserting that the normalized Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) between the rendered image and the checked-in golden PNG is within threshold.
    2. **Seeded determinism**: Verifying that two invocations with the same `--seed` produce bit-for-bit identical output images, and that different seeds produce different images.
    3. **CLI overrides & defaults**: Verifying that `--width`, `--height`, `--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`, `--color-map`, `--ipp`, and `--iterations` override the **Project** configuration as reflected in the output image dimensions and pixel values, and that omitted `proto3` fields fall back to UI defaults.
    4. **Error & warning handling**: Verifying non-zero exit codes for mutually exclusive flags (`--ipp` + `--iterations`, `--seed` + `--threads > 1`), unknown **Color Map** names, missing/corrupt input files, and verifying `stderr` warning output when an **Isolated Blend** is active.
- **Prior Art in the Codebase**:
  - Existing GTest suites registered via CMake `add_test` (`core_test`, `ui_storage_test`, `ui_models_test`) provide the pattern for CTest integration and Qt/GTest target configuration.

## Out of Scope

- Interactive UI changes or adding new rendering features to the Qt Quick application.
- Porting **Tone Mapping** from OpenGL GLSL to a CPU C++ implementation.
- Built-in image comparison subcommands inside the `chaoskit-render` binary itself (image comparison lives exclusively in the GTest end-to-end test target).
- Deterministic multi-threaded rendering when `--seed` is passed (passing `--seed` intentionally forces single-threaded execution).
- Wall-clock timeout stopping criteria for CLI rendering.

## Further Notes

- Architectural rationale for reusing `GLToneMapper` via an offscreen OpenGL context and per-thread `GathererTask` instances (switching to single-threaded execution on `--seed`) is recorded in ADR-0004 (*Headless CLI Rendering via Shared Offscreen OpenGL and Per-Thread Gathering*).

title: Prefactor shared Color Map registry and GLToneMapper zero-hit guard
description:
## Parent

- `chaoskit-q6g`

## What to build

Unify built-in **Color Map** registration in the core `ColorMapRegistry` so that both the interactive Qt UI and headless CLI tools have access to the complete set of built-in **Color Maps** (`BlackWhite`, `Rainbow`, and `BGR`) without duplicating registration in application entry points, and guard the OpenGL **Tone Mapping** shader (`GLToneMapper`) against `0.0 / 0.0` (`NaN`) evaluation when rendering pixels with zero accumulated **Histogram** hits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Constructing a `core::ColorMapRegistry` registers `"BGR"` alongside `"BlackWhite"` and `"Rainbow"`, and the UI application entry point no longer registers `"BGR"` inline.
- [ ] `ColorMapRegistry::defaultName()` preserves its content-agnostic invariant (or guarantees a valid default **Color Map** name from the registry) when a **Project**'s **Color Map** name is empty.
- [ ] In `GLToneMapper`'s fragment shader, pixels with no accumulated **Particle** hits (`point.w <= 0.0`) output opaque black `vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` early without evaluating `0.0 / 0.0` (`NaN`).
- [ ] Automated tests in `core_test` verify that `core::ColorMapRegistry` provides `"BlackWhite"`, `"Rainbow"`, and `"BGR"`, and all existing test suites pass.

title: Tracer bullet: Seeded single-threaded chaoskit-render and golden-image E2E test harness
description:
## Parent

- `chaoskit-q6g`

## What to build

Build the initial end-to-end `chaoskit-render <input-project> <output-image> [--seed <uint64>]` CLI executable in a top-level `cli` module along with the `cli_test` end-to-end golden-image test suite. Given a **Project** file in either binary `.ck` or Protobuf text format, `chaoskit-render` normalizes unset `proto3` fields using the Qt UI's defaults, lowers the **System** via `toCameraSystem` (reporting any lowering or **Isolated Blend** warnings to `stderr`), steps **Particles** on a single thread using a seeded PCG `core::Rng` into `GathererTask`, runs `GLToneMapper` against an offscreen OpenGL 3.2 Core framebuffer, and writes the rendered image to disk.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `chaoskit-render <input-project> <output-image>` loads both binary Protobuf `.ck` files and human-readable Protobuf `TextFormat` files, failing with a non-zero exit code and diagnostic message if the file cannot be read or parsed.
- [ ] Unset/zero `proto3` fields on a loaded **Project** default to `width = 1024`, `height = 1024`, `gamma = 2.2`, and `ColorMapRegistry::defaultName()` when `color_map.name` is empty; an unrecognized non-empty `color_map.name` exits non-zero.
- [ ] Lowering warnings from `toCameraSystem`—plus an explicit warning when `isolated_blend` is set on the **System**—are printed to `stderr`.
- [ ] Passing `--seed <uint64>` runs **Particle** simulation deterministically on a single thread using a PCG-backed `core::Rng`, plotting `100 * width * height` plotted steps (`process()` + `processCamera()`) into `GathererTask` and tone-mapping via `GLToneMapper` on an offscreen OpenGL 3.2 Core framebuffer with vertical orientation matching the Qt UI's `SystemView`.
- [ ] `cli_test` invokes `chaoskit-render` at the CLI seam to verify bitwise determinism for repeated `--seed` runs, error and warning diagnostics, and end-to-end golden-image comparison via normalized RMSE (supporting `CHAOSKIT_UPDATE_GOLDENS=1` and writing `<test>_actual.png` and `<test>_diff.png` on failure).

title: Multi-threaded Histogram gathering and workload flags (--threads, --ipp, --iterations)
description:
## Parent

- `chaoskit-q6g`

## What to build

Enable fast multi-threaded **Particle** simulation and **Histogram** accumulation by default in `chaoskit-render` when `--seed` is omitted, and add workload and concurrency CLI flags (`--threads <N>`, `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>`, and `--iterations <N>`). Worker threads step **Particles** into thread-local `GathererTask` **Histogram** buffers without lock contention and sum the buffers into a single **Histogram** before **Tone Mapping**, while passing `--seed` automatically switches execution to single-threaded deterministic mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When `--seed` is omitted, `chaoskit-render` defaults to running across `std::thread::hardware_concurrency()` worker threads (minimum 1, or `--threads <N>` when specified), each accumulating into its own thread-local `GathererTask` **Histogram** buffer merged by summation on completion.
- [ ] When `--seed` is passed, `chaoskit-render` runs on a single thread; passing both `--seed` and `--threads` greater than 1 fails with a non-zero exit code and error message.
- [ ] `--ipp <N>` / `--iterations-per-pixel <N>` (default `100`) sets the total plotted step budget to `N * width * height`, and `--iterations <N>` sets an exact total plotted step budget; passing both `--ipp` and `--iterations` fails with a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] `cli_test` verifies multi-threaded golden-image rendering (within normalized RMSE threshold), workload flag behavior (`--ipp` and `--iterations`), and error handling for invalid or conflicting `--threads`, `--seed`, `--ipp`, and `--iterations` arguments.

title: CLI Project override flags (--width, --height, --gamma, --exposure, --vibrancy, --color-map)
description:
## Parent

- `chaoskit-q6g`

## What to build

Add CLI override flags (`--width`, `--height`, `--gamma`, `--exposure`, `--vibrancy`, and `--color-map`) to `chaoskit-render` so developers can override image dimensions, **Tone Mapping** parameters, and the active **Color Map** on top of a loaded **Project** from the command line without editing the **Project** file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Passing `--width <uint>` and/or `--height <uint>` overrides the loaded **Project**'s dimensions (and scales the `--ipp` plotted-step budget and output image size accordingly); non-positive or non-numeric dimension arguments fail with a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Passing `--gamma <float>`, `--exposure <float>`, and/or `--vibrancy <float>` overrides the loaded **Project**'s **Tone Mapping** settings before executing `GLToneMapper`; non-positive `--gamma` or malformed float values fail with a non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Passing `--color-map <name>` overrides the loaded **Project**'s **Color Map** selection, failing with a non-zero exit code if `<name>` is not registered in `ColorMapRegistry`.
- [ ] `cli_test` verifies at the CLI seam that each override flag visibly takes effect in the rendered output image and that invalid override values return a non-zero exit code.

title: Remove obsolete initial_transform field from chaoskit.proto
description: System.initial_transform in ui/storage/chaoskit.proto is an orphaned field from the removed SimpleInterpreter (superseded by SystemProcessor::Bounds). Remove initial_transform (and reserve tag 4) from chaoskit.proto.

title: Fix SystemProcessor lifetime warm-up and initial randomization
description: When Lifetime is [Min, Max], SystemProcessor::createParticle() randomizes ttl in [1, Max] instead of [Min + 1, Max], allowing a particle that dies before Min to be returned and plotted by BlenderTask before completing Min warm-up steps. Additionally, the warm-up loop in SystemProcessor::process() (for (; output.skip >= 0; --output.skip)) runs Min + 1 iterations instead of Min unplotted warm-up iterations on revival.
